question: In MTIC carousel fraud, what does a contra-trading scheme add on top of the basic carousel, and which commodity is identified as an emerging one in VAT fraud schemes?
summary: Per Europol's EU-SOCTA 2025, contra-trading is described as the most complex and emerging form of MTIC carousel fraud: criminal networks insert an extra layer of companies to create a second trading circuit (a second carousel) on top of the basic circular scheme, representing the culmination of the complexity used to obscure connections between participants. On commodities, precious metals — including gold — are identified as an emerging commodity in VAT fraud schemes, exploited through misdeclaration (while electronics/mobile phones, IT goods, food and beverages and luxury second-hand cars remain the most commonly reported).

claims.text: Carousel fraud is the most common form of MTIC fraud and involves a circular trading scheme in which the same goods are repeatedly imported and exported across multiple Member States, with VAT refunds claimed for taxes that were never paid.

The contra-trading scheme is described as the most complex and emerging scheme of MTIC carousel fraud, in which criminal networks add an extra layer of companies to create a second trading circuit or carousel.
MTIC fraud inherently relies on complex networks of companies to obscure connections between participants, a level of complexity culminating in contra-trading schemes.
Precious metals, including gold, are identified as an emerging commodity in VAT fraud schemes, exploited through misdeclaration.

Commodities frequently targeted in carousel fraud include IT goods and accessories, high-demand food and beverage products, and luxury second-hand cars, due to the difficulty of tracking their movement through supply chains.
Electronic products, particularly mobile phones, are among the most widely reported commodities involved in VAT fraud schemes.
